rules.title: San Diego Just Cause Required for Termination of Tenancy
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without just cause. At-fault causes include nonpayment, lease breach, nuisance and criminal activity. No-fault causes include owner or family move-in, withdrawal from the rental market, government or court orders to vacate, and demolition or substantial remodel. Tenants must receive written notices stating the cause.

coverage_conditions.summary: Residential rental property in the City of San Diego for tenancies over 30 days, excluding housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years and the other listed exemptions.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Exempt if the landlord is not a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member, or mobilehome park management, the unit is alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit, and the tenant received the required written exemption notice. Also exempt: owner-occupied single-family residences renting no more than two bedrooms, ADUs or JADUs, and owner-occupied two-unit properties.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Tenancy excludes fixed-term leases of three months or less. Exempt: affordable deed-restricted or subsidized housing (Section 8 is not exempt), mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law, hotels, short-term rentals, care facilities, dormitories and shared-facility rentals with a resident landlord.  Housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years is exempt unless it is a mobilehome.  Mobilehomes are not subject to the 15-year exemption.  Non-profit transitional housing is exempt.  Tenant is a natural person.  Landlord must give notice of the exemption in the lease for tenancies commenced or renewed on or after 2024-01-01.  ADUs are covered when not exempt.  Section 8 tenancies remain covered.  Exempt units include housing restricted as affordable by deed or regulatory agreement.  Exemption list is in §98.0703.

rules.exemptions: Transient/tourist hotels; short-term residential occupancy; deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing (not Section 8); mobilehomes under the Mobilehome Residency Law; nonprofit hospitals, religious facilities, care facilities and non-profit transitional housing; dormitories; shared bathroom/kitchen with resident landlord; owner-occupied single-family residence (up to two bedrooms/ADUs/JADUs rented); owner-occupied two-unit property; housing with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (except mobilehomes); separately alienable property not owned by a REIT, corporation, LLC with a corporate member or mobilehome park management, with written notice.
rules.interaction: Consistent with California Civil Code section 1946.2. Rights are in addition to state or federal rights. Relocation assistance is credited against other required relocation assistance.
rules.quoted_span: A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for no-fault terminations
rules.requirement: For a no-fault just cause termination, the landlord must give the tenant relocation assistance either as a direct payment within 15 days of the notice or as a rent waiver. It is owed regardless of the tenant's income or length of tenancy. The tenant receives two months of actual rent, or three months if a senior or disabled.
rules.key_value: 2 months' rent (3 months if tenant is a senior or disabled)

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenancies subject to the Division that are terminated for no-fault just cause under §98.0704(b), net of exemptions in §98.0703.
coverage_conditions.owner_conditions: Same owner-based exemptions as §98.0703 (e.g., owner-occupied properties; separately alienable property not owned by a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, with notice).
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Not owed to a tenant found by a government agency or court to be at fault for the condition triggering a vacate order under §98.0704(b)(3). Seniors are age 62 or older.

rules.interaction: Credited against any other relocation assistance required by federal, state or other local law. It is in addition to the return of any security deposit.
rules.quoted_span: (A) The landlord shall provide a direct payment to the tenant.

rules.title: Right of first offer to re-rent after no-fault eviction
rules.requirement: If a unit is offered for rent within five years after the tenant was evicted for owner move-in, government order, or demolition or remodel, the landlord must first offer it in writing to the displaced tenant who asked for the offer. The tenant has 30 days to accept, and the landlord may screen the tenant.

coverage_conditions.summary: Tenancies terminated for no-fault just cause under §98.0704(b)(1), (3) or (4) where the tenant asked in writing within 30 days of the termination notice for an offer to renew.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Tenant must provide a mailing or email address.

rules.title: Buyout agreement restrictions
rules.requirement: A landlord must give a written disclosure before making a buyout offer, and buyout agreements must be in writing with required statements. A buyout agreement for less than the tenant's relocation assistance is void, and tenants cannot waive these protections.
rules.key_value: Buyout must exceed relocation assistance (2 or 3 months' rent)

coverage_conditions.summary: Buyout offers and agreements for residential rental property subject to the Division, net of §98.0703 exemptions.
coverage_conditions.other_conditions: Buyout agreement excludes agreements settling a pending unlawful detainer action.

rules.exemptions: Same exemptions as §98.0703; agreements settling a pending unlawful detainer action are not buyout agreements.
rules.interaction: Tied to the relocation assistance amounts in §98.0706(c).
